questions.prompt: Which conjugate base is most stabilized by resonance?

feedback.hint: Look for equivalent or near-equivalent atoms that can share charge through π bonding.
feedback.solution: The acetate ion delocalizes negative charge over two oxygen atoms. The other listed anions lack comparable resonance stabilization.

questions.prompt: A tertiary alkyl halide in water undergoes substitution. Which pathway is generally more plausible?
options: SN2, because the tertiary center is unhindered
SN1, because ionization can form a stabilized carbocation
Neither pathway can occur in a protic solvent

feedback.hint: Tertiary substitution centers are strongly sterically hindered for backside attack.
feedback.solution: SN1 is generally favored for a tertiary center in a polar protic solvent because carbocation formation is stabilized and SN2 is sterically hindered. The actual pathway depends on the full substrate and conditions.

questions.prompt: Which geometric arrangement is required for a typical concerted E2 elimination?
options: Any arrangement because the carbocation rotates
A tetrahedral carbon with no beta hydrogen
An aromatic ring with all sigma bonds fixed

feedback.hint: E2 forms the π bond as the C–H and C–leaving-group bonds break together.
feedback.solution: The required orbital alignment is usually anti-periplanar; in a cyclohexane chair this is trans-diaxial.

modifications: Clarified the typical E2 answer option as anti-periplanar; atypical syn elimination is not presented as equally typical.

questions.prompt: Why are acid chlorides generally more reactive toward nucleophilic acyl substitution than amides?
options: Chloride is a better leaving group and donates less by resonance
Amide carbonyl carbon is more electrophilic

feedback.hint: Compare leaving-group basicity and resonance donation into the carbonyl.
feedback.solution: Chloride is a weaker base and better leaving group than an amide anion, while nitrogen donates strongly by resonance and reduces amide carbonyl electrophilicity.
